To remedy this, `--exec` now only allows safe conversions in its command templates. - Most users can simply replace `%(...)s` with `%(...)q` in their `--exec` argument(s). Numeric conversions are unaffected by this change. Using unsafe conversions with `--exec` poses a significant security risk. Previously, the generated file name matched the language of the title: if the title was in Chinese, the file name was in Chinese; if it was in English, the file name was in English; if it was mixed Chinese and English, the file name was mixed too. But starting from the most recent versions, even if the title is in English, the generated file name turns out in Chinese.

For example, https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=EDmR8adJRyA , the web page title shows:

### Affected version

2026-08-02/03

### Steps to reproduce the bug

1. Deploy Piped per the above, confirm all containers healthy (docker compose ps).
2. Search for and play any YouTube video.
3. Check available quality via the API directly:
   curl -s https://pipedapi.<mydomain>/streams/<video_id> | python3 -m json.tool | grep quality

### Expected behavior

The full quality ladder (up to whatever the source video actually offers — 720p/1080p/etc.) should be available, especially since bg-helper is running and correctly wired up specifically to solve this class of problem (YouTube's PO token / SABR-enforcement requirement).

### Actual behavior

Only a single stream is ever returned:

"quality": "360p",

Tested across multiple, unrelated video IDs — same result every time. No higher resolutions are offered by the API at all (not just hidden/unselectable in the frontend — confirmed directly against the backend's own /streams/ response).

### Screenshots/Screen recordings

_No response_

### Logs

## Logs
 
`bg-helper` — entire log output since container start, nothing else is ever printed (no per-request activity, no errors):
```
Server started at http://0.0.0.0:3000
```
 
`piped` (backend) — startup, followed by a real extraction failure on a different video (same symptom, different ID — included to show this isn't specific to one video):
```
Database connection is ready!
PubSub: queue size - 0 channels
Cleanup: Removed 0 old videos
An error occoured in the path: /streams/mJaWwnPoNKE
org.schabi.newpipe.extractor.stream.StreamInfo$StreamExtractException: Could not get any stream. See error variable to get further details.
	at org.schabi.newpipe.extractor.stream.StreamInfo.extractStreams(StreamInfo.java:189)
	at org.schabi.newpipe.extractor.stream.StreamInfo.getInfo(StreamInfo.java:99)
	at org.schabi.newpipe.extractor.stream.StreamInfo.getInfo(StreamInfo.java:89)
	at org.schabi.newpipe.extractor.stream.StreamInfo.getInfo(StreamInfo.java:83)
	at me.kavin.piped.server.handlers.StreamHandlers.lambda$streamsResponse$0(StreamHandlers.java:54)
	at java.base/java.util.concurrent.FutureTask.run(FutureTask.java:317)
	at java.base/java.lang.VirtualThread.run(VirtualThread.java:329)
```
 
Note this particular video (`mJaWwnPoNKE`) fails extraction entirely (no stream at all, not even 360p), while other videos tested (e.g. the one used in the quality comparison above) do extract successfully but capped at 360p — suggesting at least two distinct failure modes are in play, both plausibly tied to the same underlying PO token/SABR problem.
 
`curl -vk` against the instance's own HTTPS endpoint, confirming this isn't a TLS/network issue — the backend itself is reachable and responding normally, just with degraded stream data:
```
< HTTP/1.1 200 OK
< Server: nginx/1.31.3
< Content-Type: text/html
```
 
## Question
 
Is there additional `bg-helper` configuration needed beyond `BG_HELPER_URL` to get it actually generating/applying valid PO tokens, or is this simply the current known state of `bg-helper-server`'s development? Happy to provide more logs/debug output if useful — `bg-helper`'s own logs currently only show its startup line with nothing per-request, so pointers on how to get more visibility (increased log verbosity, a way to confirm token generation succeeded/failed per-request) would also help.
 
## Related upstream threads
 
- [TeamNewPipe/NewPipe#13320](https://github.com/TeamNewPipe/NewPipe/issues/13320) — the general SABR-enforcement/360p-cap issue this is presumably downstream of.
- [TeamNewPipe/NewPipeExtractor#858](https://github.com/TeamNewPipe/NewPipeExtractor/issues/858) — active discussion redesigning the extractor's stream API with SABR as a first-class concept, suggesting a more durable fix is in progress upstream (though an in-progress branch linked there reportedly doesn't compile yet, so no ETA).
 

### Additional information

Additional context — direct comparison against Invidious
 
To rule out something specific to my own network/IP being flagged by YouTube, I stood up a self-hosted Invidious instance (official production Docker Compose + the required **Invidious companion** sidecar, `quay.io/invidious/invidious-companion:latest`) on the *same NAS, same network, same outbound IP*, and tested the **identical video ID**:
 
```

```
 
Result — full ladder returned:

```
"qualityLabel": "360p",
"qualityLabel": "480p",
"qualityLabel": "720p",
"qualityLabel": "1080p",
"qualityLabel": "1440p",
"qualityLabel": "2160p",
```
 
This strongly suggests the SABR/PO-token bypass is achievable from this exact network/IP — Invidious's companion is succeeding at it, while Piped's `bg-helper` is not, despite being correctly configured and running without errors.
 
I'm aware `bg-helper-server`'s own README currently marks itself `# WIP` ("This will be a server that can be used to generate PoTokens" — future tense), so this may simply be a maturity gap rather than a misconfiguration on my end. Filing this in case it's useful as a concrete, reproducible data point (exact config, versions, and a working counter-example on the same network) for whoever's working on this.

Is there additional `bg-helper` configuration needed beyond `BG_HELPER_URL` to get it actually generating/applying valid PO tokens, or is this simply the current known state of `bg-helper-server`'s development? issues.title: [Bug]: SearchClient.search throws FormatException on abbreviated "Streamed 3y ago" upload dates
issues.body:
### What happened?

### Description

`YoutubeExplode().search.search(query)` throws a `FormatException` when a result's `publishedTimeText` uses YouTube's new **abbreviated** relative-date format combined with the `Streamed` prefix (e.g. `Streamed 3y ago`).

Because the parsing happens inside the `.map(...)` that builds the `VideoSearchList`, a single affected result makes the **whole search fail**.

YouTube currently returns both formats (probably an A/B test). On the same query I get either:
- `3 years ago` / `Streamed 3 years ago` (long format, parsed correctly)
- `1y ago` / `5y ago` (abbreviated format)

### Stack trace

```
FormatException: Invalid radix-10 number (at character 1)
Streamed
^
#0  int._handleFormatError (dart:core-patch/integers_patch.dart:150:5)
#1  int._parseRadix (dart:core-patch/integers_patch.dart:179:14)
#2  int._parse (dart:core-patch/integers_patch.dart:121:12)
#3  int.parse (dart:core-patch/integers_patch.dart:81:12)
#4  StringUtility2.toDateTime (package:youtube_explode_dart/src/extensions/helpers_extension.dart:185:21)
#5  SearchClient.search.<anonymous closure> (package:youtube_explode_dart/src/search/search_client.dart:33:28)
...
#11 SearchClient.search (package:youtube_explode_dart/src/search/search_client.dart:44:12)
```

### Reproduction

```dart
import 'package:youtube_explode_dart/src/extensions/helpers_extension.dart';

void main() {
  for (final s in ['3 years ago', 'Streamed 3 years ago', '3y ago', 'Streamed 3y ago']) {
    try {
      print('"$s" -> ${s.toDateTime()}');
    } catch (e) {
      print('"$s" -> THROWS $e');
    }
  }
}
```

Output:
```
"3 years ago" -> 2023-09-24 21:24:41.397053
"Streamed 3 years ago" -> 2023-09-24 21:24:41.399590
"3y ago" -> null
"Streamed 3y ago" -> THROWS FormatException: Invalid radix-10 number (at character 1)
```

### Root cause

In `StringUtility2.toDateTime`, the `Streamed` prefix is only stripped when the string has exactly 4 parts:

```dart
var parts = this!.trim().split(' ');
if (parts.length == 4) {
  // Streamed x y ago
  parts = parts.skip(1).toList();
}
if (parts.length != 3) {
  return null;
}
final qty = int.parse(parts.first); // "Streamed" -> FormatException
```

With the abbreviated format:
- `Streamed 3y ago` has 3 parts, so the prefix isn't stripped and `int.parse('Streamed')` throws.
- `3y ago` has 2 parts, so it silently returns `null` (the upload date is lost).

### Suggested fix

- Strip the `Streamed` prefix based on the first word rather than on the part count.
- Support the abbreviated units (e.g. with a regex like `^(\d+)\s*([a-z]+)`): `s`, `m`/`min`, `h`, `d`, `w`, `mo`, `y`. I've only seen `y` so far; the other abbreviations are my guess.
- Use `int.tryParse` and return `null` instead of throwing, so one unparseable date can't break the whole search.

issues.body:
你好，感谢维护这个项目！

我最近在 Windows 上使用 `xiaohongshu-mcp v2.5.5`，尝试通过 OpenAI Secure MCP Tunnel 接入 ChatGPT。原始 MCP 服务在本地可以正常启动，并显示已注册完整工具集，但在 ChatGPT 侧创建 MCP / App 时会直接失败，界面没有给出可用于排查的具体原因。

因为缺少明确的报错信息，我们只能逐步排查接入链路。期间调整了若干与协议兼容相关的细节，最后在原 MCP 服务前增加了一个轻量兼容代理后，ChatGPT 才能够成功创建并调用。

当前结构大致是：

```
ChatGPT
  ↓
Secure MCP Tunnel
  ↓
兼容代理
  ↓
xiaohongshu-mcp v2.5.5
```

目前兼容代理只暴露了一部分只读工具，因此搜索、查看笔记详情、读取评论、查看用户主页等功能可以正常使用；点赞、收藏、评论、发布等写入工具暂时还没有接入 ChatGPT。

这里暂时无法确认问题究竟来自：
- ChatGPT / Secure MCP Tunnel 对某些 MCP 响应、初始化流程或 tool schema 的兼容要求；
- 当前版本服务端的某个协议细节；
- 还是我们自己的接入方式还有遗漏。

想请教一下：这个项目目前是否测试过 ChatGPT / OpenAI Secure MCP Tunnel？是否有已知的兼容性注意事项，或者推荐的接入方式？

如果有帮助，我们可以继续补充：
- 兼容代理的行为说明；
- 原生接入失败与兼容代理成功后的差异；

issues.title: 回复评论两处误判：定位兜底会回复到同用户的其他评论；带表情码的内容必报「未确认成功」
issues.body:
## 现象

真实使用中连续遇到两个问题（同一次使用复现，均源码级定位）：

### 1. `reply_comment_in_feed` 定位兜底导致回复挂错目标

回复某条**子评论**时，若该子评论折叠在「展开 N 条回复」里尚未渲染，`lookupComment` 的 `#comment-{id}` 选择器落空，随后按 userID 兜底扫描 `.comment-item`。当**目标子评论的作者同时也是该楼层一级评论的作者**时（很常见：楼主在自己楼里追问别人），兜底会先命中他的一级评论，回复被提交到一级评论下，观感上是"回复了楼主"而不是"回复了提问"。

### 2. 内容带表情码时必报「未确认成功」（实际已发出）

`waitCommentRendered` 用 `innerText.includes(全文)` 校验是否渲染。但 `[笑哭R]` 等表情码在页面上渲染为**图片**，不出现在 innerText 中 → 只要内容带表情码，即使发布成功也必然报错。

实测数据：5 次带表情码的发布全部误报（事后核实均已发出，其中一次差点因此重复发送）；1 次不带表情码的发布干净通过。且同函数的 `findCommentElement` 依赖「展开楼中楼」后重查，表情码问题与问题 1 叠加时，会诱导使用者手动重发，造成重复评论风险。

## 原因（comment_feed.go）

- `lookupComment`：commentID 选择器未命中后按 `[data-user-id]` 兜底，未校验命中元素是否就是目标评论本身
- `commentRendered`：`innerText.includes(txt)` 对表情码必然失配

## 修复建议

1. `lookupComment`：commentID 非空时**不做 userID 兜底**，直接返回 nil 交给上层 `findCommentElement` 的滚动+展开循环重查（该循环本身就是为此设计的）；userID 兜底仅保留给未提供 commentID 的调用
2. `commentRendered`：匹配前剥离 `[...]` 表情码（两边都剥或只剥期望文本即可）

补丁已备好（两处共 ~15 行），确认后我可以提 PR。

issues.title: 建议在点击发布前检查页面上的发布前置阻断提示
issues.body:
当账号不满足发布前置条件时（实测为**未绑定手机号**），小红书创作平台会在发布页顶部显示常驻横幅：

> 你还未绑定手机号，前往APP端「设置」-「账户与安全」-「手机号」绑定手机号后才可发布笔记

此时发布按钮**可见、未禁用、可命中**，点击也确实被按钮收到，但前端在前置校验处直接返回，不会发出任何提交请求。当前流程的表现是：点击发布 → 等待 15 秒未跳转 → 报错 `发布未确认成功：点击发布后未跳转离开发布页（可能校验未过或被拦截）`。

我们据此排查了四轮才定位到原因，期间逐一排除了坐标命中、点击后弹窗、按钮禁用、可见范围设置、图片上传未完成等可能。实测数据（在同一次尝试中依次尝试三种输入）：

| 输入方式 | 按钮收到的事件 | `isTrusted` | 该窗口内提交请求 | `submit-loading` 变化 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 鼠标坐标点击 | pointerdown → pointerup → click | true | 无 | 无（488 次连续采样） |
| 键盘 Enter | keydown → click → keyup | true | 无 | 无 |
| shadow root 内 JS `.click()` | click | false | 无 | 无 |

也就是说：事件确实到达了正确的按钮，而应用从未尝试提交——这与"被拦截"或"点击失败"都不同，是**前置条件不满足**。

建议：在点击发布之前检查页面上的阻断类横幅（这类提示出现在发布页顶部，属于静态元素而非点击后的浮层），命中则直接返回明确错误并附上提示原文。这样使用者能一眼看到「未绑定手机号」，而不是收到一句语义模糊的「未跳转离开发布页」。
